tasks.title: Scaffold Cursor Extension Structure
tasks.description: Create the `integrations/cursor-limux/` directory with package.json, extension manifest, and entry point using only Node built-ins and VS Code API.
tasks.details: Create `integrations/cursor-limux/package.json` with `main` pointing to `extension.js`. Set `engines.vscode` to compatible version. Add `activationEvents` with `onView:limux` for lazy activation. Add `contributes.views` with a Limux sidebar view. Ensure zero `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, and no package-manager scripts. Create `extension.js` with `activate()` and `deactivate()` stubs.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify `package.json` parses with no dependencies. Validate manifest schema. Run a manual smoke test with `cursor --extensionDevelopmentPath integrations/cursor-limux` to confirm the extension loads without errors.

tasks.title: Implement Socket Resolution Logic
tasks.description: Implement Limux socket path resolution mirroring the exact order: `limux.socketPath`, `LIMUX_SOCKET`, `LIMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, `LIMUX_CHANNEL` channel-derived stable/preview sockets, `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/limux/limux.sock`, then `/tmp/limux.sock`.
tasks.details: Create `socket-resolver.js`. Implement a function `resolveSocketCandidates()` returning an ordered array of candidate paths based on the PRD-specified order. Do not add `/run/user/${uid}/limux/limux.sock`. Channel-aware candidates must match `RuntimeChannel::from_env()`: `stable` maps to `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/limux/stable/limux.sock` or `/tmp/limux-stable.sock`; `preview` maps to `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/limux/preview/default/limux.sock` unless `LIMUX_PREVIEW_ID` is set; `preview:<id>` and `preview/<id>` map to `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/limux/preview/<id>/limux.sock` or `/tmp/limux-preview-<id>.sock` when `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unavailable. For each candidate, implement `probeSocket(path, timeout)` using Node `net.connect` with a timeout, sending a `system.identify` request. Return `{ connected, identity, error }`. Handle stale socket files, connection refused, and timeout explicitly.
tasks.testStrategy: Write Node tests using `node --test` covering: channel-aware resolution order, stable channel sockets, preview default and explicit ID sockets, live socket, stale file, refused connection, timeout, duplicate live sockets, and ambiguous identity. Verify the exact resolution order matches Limux source.

subtasks.title: Add channel-aware runtime socket resolution
subtasks.description: Supersedes the parent task resolver order where it omits LIMUX_CHANNEL.
subtasks.details: Resolver order must be: Cursor setting limux.socketPath, LIMUX_SOCKET, LIMUX_SOCKET_PATH, LIMUX_CHANNEL channel-derived sockets matching RuntimeChannel::from_env(), then the XDG_RUNTIME_DIR legacy default, then /tmp/limux.sock. stable maps to XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/limux/stable/limux.sock or /tmp/limux-stable.sock. preview maps to XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/limux/preview/default/limux.sock unless LIMUX_PREVIEW_ID is set. preview:<id> or preview/<id> maps to XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/limux/preview/<id>/limux.sock or /tmp/limux-preview-<id>.sock when XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unavailable. Do not add /run/user/${uid}/limux/limux.sock as a separate Cursor fallback unless Limux source adds it first.

tasks.title: Implement Limux Socket Framing Client
tasks.description: Create a Node `net.connect`-based client implementing the existing Limux JSON framing protocol for request/response communication over Unix sockets.
tasks.details: Create `limux-client.js`. Implement framing according to existing Limux protocol (newline-delimited JSON or length-prefixed per current source). Implement `sendRequest(method, params, timeout)` returning a promise. Handle connection lifecycle, reconnection for refresh, and error propagation. Do not shell out for any communication.
tasks.testStrategy: Node tests for framing: valid frame round-trip, malformed frame handling, timeout, connection drop mid-request. Verify no child_process usage in the client.

tasks.title: Implement Runtime Discovery and Selection
tasks.description: Build runtime discovery that probes all candidate sockets, displays identity, lets the user select among multiple live runtimes, and pins the selected identity for state-changing commands.
tasks.details: Create `runtime-manager.js`. Use socket resolver to get candidates, probe each, collect live runtimes with their `system.identify` response. If multiple, show a QuickPick with identity info. Store the selected runtime identity. Before any state-changing command, verify the current runtime identity matches the pinned identity; fail with a clear error if identity changed. Surface disconnected state clearly when no live runtime is found.
tasks.testStrategy: Node tests: single live runtime auto-selects, multiple runtimes trigger choice, stale/timeout surfaces disconnected state, identity change on pinned runtime causes state-changing command to fail.

tasks.title: Define Shared Restricted Method Allowlist
tasks.description: Create a shared, pinned method allowlist exactly matching `workspace.list`, `workspace.select`, `window.present`, `cursor.pane_create_empty`, `surface.read_text`, and `cursor.workspace_open_folder`, shared by both Rust and extension request builders.
tasks.details: Create a shared definition (e.g., `methods.json` or a generated constant) listing the exact v1 methods. In the extension, create `request-builder.js` that can only emit requests for methods in this allowlist. Ensure request builders cannot construct `surface.send_text`, `surface.send_key`, `pane.create.command`, or any method outside the set. The Rust side must consume the same allowlist definition for enforcement.
tasks.testStrategy: Node tests verify request builders reject any non-allowlisted method. Verify the allowlist is exactly the 6 pinned methods. Cross-check Rust constant matches the shared definition.

tasks.title: Implement Server-Side Cursor-Restricted Method Surface
tasks.description: Add a server-side restricted method dispatch path in the Limux host that enforces the Cursor allowlist, rejecting forbidden methods and unexpected payload fields.
tasks.details: In `rust/limux-host-linux/src/control_bridge.rs`, add either a restricted socket path or a per-connection caller role/nonce mechanism. Implement an allowlist check before dispatch. Reject `surface.send_text`, `surface.send_key`, `pane.create.command` (command-bearing), unknown methods, and unexpected payload fields with a clear error. Implement `system.capabilities` to return the restricted method set for Cursor connections. Preserve existing unrestricted socket behavior for CLI/agent compatibility.
tasks.testStrategy: Rust tests: restricted path rejects `surface.send_text`, `surface.send_key`, raw `pane.create.command`, unknown methods, unexpected payload fields. Restricted path allows the 6 pinned methods. Unrestricted path remains compatible with existing CLI/agent methods.

tasks.title: Implement Workspace List and Tree Data Provider
tasks.description: Implement the Limux sidebar tree view with `vscode.TreeDataProvider` showing `Workspace -> Pane -> Tab/Surface` hierarchy using `workspace.list` responses.
tasks.details: Create `limux-tree-provider.js` implementing `vscode.TreeDataProvider`. Define tree item types: Workspace, Pane, Tab, Surface with stable IDs and context values. Implement `getChildren()` calling `workspace.list` via the Limux client. Implement `onDidChangeTreeData` for refresh. Handle refresh failures by showing a disconnected state in the tree. Use `onDidChangeConfiguration` for socket path changes. Register the provider in `extension.js` activate().
tasks.testStrategy: Node tests for TreeDataProvider: tree shape correctness, stable IDs, refresh triggers `onDidChangeTreeData`, disconnected state on refresh failure. Manual smoke test verifies tree displays against a running Limux.

tasks.title: Implement Workspace Select and Window Present
tasks.description: Implement `workspace.select` (selection-only) and `window.present` (best-effort raise/focus) with explicit result states and Wayland limitation surfacing.
tasks.details: Add command handlers for `workspace.select` and `window.present` in the extension. `workspace.select` is selection-only, no side effects. `window.present` returns `succeeded`, `failed`, or `unsupported`. On Wayland, surface limitations to the user via a notification or status bar message rather than silently failing. Document Wayland focus constraints in extension UI. Add Rust implementation for `window.present` with X11/Wayland detection.
tasks.testStrategy: Rust tests for `window.present` covering success, failure, unsupported. Extension tests for command invocation and result handling. Xvfb smoke test for available presentation behavior. Manual Wayland smoke required before claiming Wayland focus support.

tasks.title: Implement Empty Pane Creation
tasks.description: Implement `cursor.pane_create_empty` in both Rust host and extension, rejecting any command, text, key, paste, shell, or raw PTY payload fields.
tasks.details: Rust: add `cursor.pane_create_empty` handler in control_bridge that validates the payload contains no `command`, `text`, `key`, `paste`, `shell`, or PTY fields. Reject any unexpected field. Create an empty pane only. Extension: add a request builder and command that invokes `cursor.pane_create_empty` with an empty or minimal payload. Ensure the builder cannot emit command-bearing creation.
tasks.testStrategy: Rust tests: submit hand-crafted JSON frames with forbidden fields (`command`, `text`, `key`, `paste`, `shell`) and prove rejection. Verify clean empty payload succeeds. Extension tests: verify request builder only emits allowed fields.

tasks.title: Implement Safe Path Determination and Folder Opening
tasks.description: Implement `workspace.list` path metadata (`folder_path`, `openable_path`, `path_source`) with canonicalization checks, and implement bidirectional folder opening between Limux and Cursor with strict safety validation.
tasks.details: Rust: implement safe path determination requiring canonicalized, existing local directories. Expose `folder_path`, `openable_path`, `path_source` in `workspace.list`. Implement `cursor.workspace_open_folder` accepting only local `file:` folders in same Linux/Remote-WSL host. Reject native Windows paths, virtual folders, remote folders, untitled folders, ambiguous multi-root. tasks.testStrategy: Rust tests: spaces, leading dashes, shell metacharacters, missing dirs, files, broken symlinks, symlink escapes. Extension tests: local folder eligibility, rejection of non-file schemes, multi-root quick-pick. Verify launcher argv construction has no shell interpolation.

tasks.title: Implement Read-Only Visible Surface Snapshots

tasks.details: Rust: implement `surface.read_text` returning current visible viewport only. Bound the response size. Include explicit encoding field. No scrollback semantics. Reject requests with `count`, `offset`, scrollback, `paste`, `key`, or `text` payload fields. Extension: add a command to fetch and display the snapshot in a read-only editor panel.
tasks.testStrategy: Rust tests: bounded output size, viewport-only content, rejection of forbidden parameters (`count`, `offset`, `scrollback`, `paste`, `key`, `text`). Extension tests: snapshot display in read-only view, no input fields accepted.

tasks.title: Implement Runtime Trust: Build Identity, limux doctor, and Log Triage
tasks.description: Implement the complete PRD-A scope: compile-time build identity via build.rs in three binary crates, BuildInfo injection in limux-core, --version flag in CLI, system.identify build object on both dispatcher paths, host start-line and panic hook, install-info.json in installer, limux doctor subcommand with 5 checks and JSON schema, and log-triage classifier with ANSI stripping.
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing is multi-layered:

1. **Unit tests for pattern table** — in the pattern table source file, one test per pattern class using fixture lines lifted verbatim from the real log. Verify each fixture classifies to the correct category.

2. **Unit tests for install-info parsing** — test parsing of valid, absent, and malformed `install-info.json` (malformed → fields omitted, no panic).

3. **Unit tests for drift evaluation logic** — pure function testing of symlink resolution, wrapper script parsing, and channel grouping logic without requiring a real filesystem.

4. **Unit tests for ANSI stripping** — verify control bytes/escape sequences are stripped from log content in triage output.

5. **Integration test for doctor** — in `rust/limux-cli/src/main.rs` test module or Xvfb harness: stage two fake install roots under a temp prefix (`LIMUX_USER_PREFIX`), point a fake `limux*` symlink→wrapper at the older root, run a copied `limux-host` binary from the newer root so `/proc/<pid>/exe` resolves there, and verify doctor detects and reports the mismatch as `warn`/`fail`.

6. **Build identity tests** — `cargo test -p limux-host-linux build_identity -- --nocapture` verifies the host start-line and panic hook carry build identity.

7. **System.identify tests** — verify `build` object appears on both standalone dispatcher and GTK bridge paths with correct shape.

8. **Full gate** — `./scripts/check.sh` must pass with no new failures vs baseline (verify baseline `hook_session_id_falls_back_to_transcript_stem` first).

9. **Smoke test** — `LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh` (extended with a doctor invocation) verifies end-to-end behavior.

10. **Installer dry-run** — `scripts/user-local-install/install-user-local.sh --dry-run --profile release --install-id prd-a-check` verifies installer changes (note: SHA256SUMS not verifiable in dry-run).

11. **Manual verification** — run `limux --version` and `limux doctor` on operator's machine to confirm stale-build condition is detected, then after clean install reports clean.

tasks.title: Implement Ghostty resource + terminfo packaging correctness in installer
tasks.description: Modify install-user-local.sh to stage valid Ghostty resources (shell-integration + compiled terminfo containing xterm-ghostty), implement identical shape validation matching runtime contract (is_ghostty_resources_dir + has_ghostty_terminfo from rust/limux-host-linux/src/main.rs:60-72), abort loudly on invalid/absent resources with explicit --allow-missing-ghostty-resources escape hatch, add manifest fields (resource shape, origin), vendor pinned ghostty.terminfo snapshot with provenance header, enumerate SHA256SUMS over all resource files, and create CI test script scripts/tests/validate-ghostty-resources.sh wired into .github/workflows/rust-quality.yml.
tasks.details:
Implementation steps:

1. VENDOR TERMINFO SOURCE:
   - Create scripts/user-local-install/resources/ghostty.terminfo with provenance header (upstream Ghostty version + generation method + date)
   - Source from Ghostty build output or documented generation via built binary +terminfo flag

2. RESOURCE PRODUCTION (install-user-local.sh):
   - Ensure ghostty submodule initialized: git submodule update --init ghostty (checkout-only, no zig build consensus gate trigger)
   - Resource priority order:
     a) If ghostty/zig-out/share/ghostty/ exists, stage from it (keep current preference)
     b) DEFAULT: compile vendored ghostty.terminfo via 'tic -x -o share/limux/terminfo/' and copy shell-integration from ghostty/src/shell-integration/ (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, nushell)
     c) Full zig build allowed but NOT required
   - Output layout (MUST match runtime contract):
     share/limux/ghostty/shell-integration/  (shell-integration inside resources dir)
     share/limux/terminfo/                   (sibling under resources dir's parent — NEVER nested inside ghostty/)
     share/limux/terminfo/x/xterm-ghostty    (compiled entry as regular file)

3. SHAPE VALIDATION FUNCTION:
   - Implement IDENTICAL contract to is_ghostty_resources_dir + has_ghostty_terminfo (rust/limux-host-linux/src/main.rs:60-72)
   - Assert: shell-integration/ directory exists inside resources dir
   - Assert: terminfo/ exists as sibling under resources dir's parent
   - Assert: terminfo/x/xterm-ghostty exists as regular file (NOT relying on tic exit code alone)
   - Add comment in both installer and main.rs referencing each other
   - Reject source-only shape (ghostty/src-style: shell-integration without compiled terminfo)

4. TIC AVAILABILITY CHECK:
   - Check tic at install time; absent -> loud abort with ncurses-bin install instructions
   - Pseudo-code:
     if ! command -v tic >/dev/null 2>&1; then
       error_exit "tic not found. Install ncurses-bin package. Aborting."
     fi

5. INSTALLER BEHAVIOR MODIFICATIONS (install-user-local.sh):
   - --apply: if no valid resource bundle -> abort with clear error naming expected shape + build step. NOT 'resources: not found' silent pass
   - --allow-missing-ghostty-resources flag: preserve old behavior, stamp manifest 'DEGRADED: no ghostty resources'
   - --dry-run: report which resource path WOULD be used + shape verdict (plan statement, no tic compile/SHA256SUMS verification)
   - Source-only shape (ghostty/src) rejected with same loud error

6. MANIFEST.md UPDATES:
   - Keep existing value shapes: 'Ghostty resources: <path>', 'Ghostty terminfo: <path>'
   - Add: 'Ghostty resource shape: valid|DEGRADED'
   - Add: 'Ghostty resource origin: <source description>'
   - CRITICAL: origin NEVER goes into 'Ghostty resources:' line (must keep grep invariant: valid install must NOT say 'Ghostty resources: .../ghostty/src')

7. SHA256SUMS ENUMERATION:
   - Replace fixed 6-file list with dynamic enumeration:
     find share/limux -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum
   - Covers variable resource file set

8. CI TEST SCRIPT (scripts/tests/validate-ghostty-resources.sh):
   - Build/stage resource bundle
   - Assert: shell-integration present
   - Assert: compiled terminfo entry FILES present (terminfo/x/xterm-ghostty as regular file)
   - Assert: infocmp -A <dir> xterm-ghostty exits 0
   - Assert: manifest fields present
   - Regression test: staged source-only directory -> installer shape check rejects it
   - Wire into .github/workflows/rust-quality.yml as explicit new step
   - ALSO wire validate-split-icons.sh into same step (currently wired into NO workflow)

9. DOCUMENTATION:
   - Append closing note to docs/terminal-input-regression-20260701.md pointing at new guardrails (don't rewrite history)
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing approach per PRD Testing Instructions:

1. RUN ALL CHECKS:
   ./scripts/check.sh  # must pass as gate per commit

2. NEW VALIDATION SCRIPT:
   bash scripts/tests/validate-ghostty-resources.sh
   - Asserts shell-integration present, compiled terminfo entry files present, infocmp succeeds, manifest fields present
   - Regression test encodes ghostty/src failure class: staged source-only dir -> installer rejects

3. DRY-RUN VERIFICATION:
   scripts/user-local-install/install-user-local.sh --dry-run --channel preview --profile release --install-id prd-b-check
   - Reports which resource path WOULD be used + shape verdict

4. APPLY INSTALL:
   scripts/user-local-install/install-user-local.sh --apply --channel preview --profile release --install-id prd-b-check
   - Must complete with valid resources (no 'resources: not found' silent pass)

5. VERIFY TERMINFO:
   infocmp -A ~/.local/limux-reviewed/preview/default/prd-b-check/share/limux/terminfo xterm-ghostty
   - Must exit 0
   test -f ~/.local/limux-reviewed/preview/default/prd-b-check/share/limux/terminfo/x/xterm-ghostty
   - Must be regular file

6. SMOKE TEST:
   LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh
   - Optional harness extension: target install root via LIMUX_HOST_BIN override + read-screen assertion on 'echo $TERM'
   - Fallback: repo-build proxy (staged resources + GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR pointed at staged bundle)
   - Acceptance: TERM=xterm-ghostty resolved, no ?-prompt-byte corruption

7. MANIFEST VERIFICATION:
   - grep 'Ghostty resources:' MANIFEST.md must NOT match '.../ghostty/src'
   - 'Ghostty resource shape: valid' field present
   - 'Ghostty resource origin: <source description>' field present

8. DEGRADED MODE:
   - install-user-local.sh --apply --allow-missing-ghostty-resources --install-id degraded-test
   - Must complete with 'DEGRADED: no ghostty resources' marker in manifest

9. SOURCE-ONLY REJECTION:
   - Stage ghostty/src-style directory (shell-integration without compiled terminfo)
   - Run installer --apply
   - Must abort with loud error, same message shape as runtime check

10. SHA256SUMS COVERAGE:
    - Verify SHA256SUMS covers all resource files (find share/limux -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum style)

On full PASS, promote via scripts/user-local-install/install-user-local.sh --apply --profile release --channel stable --install-id <verified-sha-id> from the same source SHA; on any FAIL, record verdict + evidence, block promotion, and file/reopen TaskMaster tasks.
tasks.details:
1. Create directory scaffold: docs/verification/, docs/verification/runs/ (with .gitkeep), docs/verification/run-template.md.
2. Author docs/verification/post-install-checklist-v1.md with:
   - Header block for build SHA + install-id (from `limux --version`), date, operator verdict per item.
   - Setup section: exact copy-paste commands to install preview-channel build from current origin/main, launch, and run checklist. Must use `--channel preview` explicitly (per runtime-channel-contract) so the operator's daily driver (stable) is never displaced.
   - Numbered steps, each: exact action → expected result → PASS/FAIL checkbox.
   - Cover at minimum:
     a) Plain typing + modifier chords + paste in a fresh pane (#14 class): verify `Ctrl+Shift+V` performs Limux terminal paste, while plain `Ctrl+V` is intentionally unclaimed by Limux and passes through to terminal/native shell behavior (matches default_terminal_paste_does_not_claim_plain_ctrl_v).
     b) Mouse selection-copy → paste elsewhere, verifying no stuck-left-click state (the LIFO_HANDOFF.md watch item).
     c) Window controls (minimize/maximize/close) + edge hitbox (#15 class).
     d) Drag-resize soak ≥30 s while a live agent TUI (claude or codex) is running (resize-storm class).
     e) Sidebar resize handle + collapse/restore.
     f) Close-and-relaunch session restore of a multi-workspace layout.
     g) `limux notify` toast + sidebar dot.
     h) `limux doctor` reports clean/no-drift.
     i) Runtime-channel isolation smoke: run scripts/tests/runtime-isolation-smoke.sh; operator confirms stable + preview windows behave simultaneously without socket interference.
   - Inline the normative three-row symptom-split table exactly:
     | Symptom | Likely class |
     |---|---|
     | Typing corrupted / keys act as shortcuts | keyboard-modifier (#14) or Ghostty resource shape (PRD-B) |
     | `?` / boxed glyphs in prompt | environmental font (Nerd Font / Powerlevel10k) — NOT a Limux input bug |
     | `00~...01~` around pasted text | bracketed-paste shell mode — NOT a Limux input bug |
   - State the write-back rule: a fix PR that changes operator-visible behavior is not `done` until a checklist run (full or relevant subset) records its verdict.
   - State the versioning rule: v1 frozen after first run; edits create v2; runs reference the version they executed.
   - State the promotion rule (exact operation): if ALL items PASS on a FULL run (subset runs may close individual tasks but NEVER promote), lifo promotes by running `scripts/user-local-install/install-user-local.sh --apply --profile release --channel stable --install-id <verified-sha-id>` from the SAME source SHA the preview run verified. Promotion is a fresh stable-channel install of the verified source, not a symlink hand-edit. Operator relaunches from the stable launcher.
   - Resolve the launcher-name question at authoring time: the operator's current daily launcher is the LEGACY name (~/.local/bin/limux); the checklist doc must state which launcher name the operator uses post-promotion (limux-stable) OR include the explicit legacy-launcher update step. Capture the resolution in the checklist doc.
   - On any FAIL: record verdict + evidence, block promotion, file a new TaskMaster task via `task-master-reviewed add-task`, reopen existing tasks via `task-master-reviewed set-status --id <n> --status pending` with an evidence note. For #14 FAIL, capture `LIMUX_DEBUG_KEYS=1` log.
3. Author docs/verification/run-template.md: a copy-paste template for run files, including header fields (build SHA, install-id, date, checklist version + its git SHA, operator, per-item verdict table, overall verdict, promotion decision).
4. Execute the first live checklist run:
   - [USER] Operator installs preview-channel build from current origin/main and executes checklist v1 (~10 min).
   - Save the filled checklist to docs/verification/runs/<date>-<install-id>.md (committed). Run file must record the checklist file's git SHA.
   - Append FYI.md entry: What/Why/How/Impact + link to the run file.
   - Update TaskMaster via `task-master-reviewed set-status` for every task the run confirms or reopens:
     - #14 (typing/modifier/paste): record verdict; stays `done` or reopened with evidence.
     - #15 (window controls): record verdict; `review` → `done` or reopened.
     - Resize-soak, sidebar-handle, session-restore, stuck-click/selection-copy: record verdicts.
     - Runtime-channel isolation smoke: scripted part + operator confirmation.
   - If ALL PASS on full run: run the exact promotion command from the same source SHA; operator relaunches from stable launcher.
   - If any FAIL: block promotion, file/reopen tasks as specified.
5. Optional harness assist (skip if PRD-A has no room or is not yet landed): add `--checklist-header` flag to `limux doctor` printing the build/install/date block for pasting into a run file. Manual copy is acceptable for v1.
6. Ensure ./scripts/check.sh passes (docs-mostly PRD).

tasks.title: Implement pane attention border overlay fix and per-pane color flag system
tasks.description: Fix the pane attention border rendering behind pane content by migrating to a top-overlay GtkOverlay child widget, and add a deterministic per-pane color flag system with pane.action bridge routing, session persistence, CLI access, and context-menu GUI affordance.
tasks.testStrategy:
## Unit Tests

### Attention Border Overlay (US-1)
1. **Widget-tree z-order test**: Assert the attention overlay indicator is an `add_overlay` child of the pane's `content_overlay` (which is already a `gtk::Overlay`). Verify overlay z-order places it above the GLArea terminal content.
2. **`set_can_target(false)` assertion**: Verify the overlay indicator widget has `can_target == false` so clicks pass through to terminal.
3. **Opacity independence test**: Assert the overlay widget's opacity property is opaque (1.0), independent of `sanitize_background_opacity` path.
4. **Guard test update**: Extend `pane_attention_css_targets_content_overlay_not_outer_shell` (pane.rs:3583) to assert:
   - OLD `.limux-pane-attention` class still ABSENT
   - NEW overlay widget exists as `add_overlay` child
   - Overlay has `can_target == false`
5. **Hover-clear regression test**: Verify existing timer semantics preserved — hover triggers clear, no change to auto-clear behavior.
6. **No Gtk-CRITICAL**: Assert no `Gtk-CRITICAL` output across the Xvfb suite.

### Flag Color State (US-2, US-3)
7. **Semantic separation test**: Setting/clearing `flag_color` never mutates attention state and vice versa.
8. **Unread styling regression test**: Setting a flag color does not change unread dot/styling on the sidebar/tab path.
9. **Allowlist validation test**: Invalid color strings → clean error, no partial state. Valid colors from `{red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple}` accepted.
10. **Session persistence test**: `flag_color` survives save to session.json and restore on relaunch. Older builds without the field load safely (serde defaults, no `deny_unknown_fields`).
11. **pane.action core test**: `cargo test -p limux-core pane_action` — verify `PaneAction::SetFlagColor` and `PaneAction::ClearFlagColor` dispatch correctly.
12. **pane.list metadata test**: `pane.list` rows include pane-scoped `flag_color`. `pane.surfaces` may mirror as `pane_flag_color` (redundant context only). No per-surface/per-tab `flag_color` field.
13. **No existing fields renamed**: Assert no field name changes in pane metadata.

### Integration / Smoke
14. **Xvfb smoke test**: `LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh` extended with flag-color + attention-overlay assertions.
15. **Layout regression**: Verify for single pane, H-split right pane, V-split bottom pane, nested 3-pane layout, and after drag-resizing the split — primary acceptance is widget-tree unit test asserting overlay z-order.

### Gate
```bash
./scripts/check.sh   # no NEW failures vs baseline
cargo test -p limux-host-linux attention -- --nocapture
cargo test -p limux-host-linux flag_color -- --nocapture
cargo test -p limux-core pane_action -- --nocapture
```

### Primary Acceptance Criteria
- Widget-tree unit test asserting the overlay z-order (overlay indicator is an `add_overlay` child of the pane's `content_overlay`).
- Operator confirms attention border is clearly visible on a right-hand split pane (PRD-C checklist).
- Color flags survive a full close/relaunch cycle.

### Do NOT use for verification
- `debug.window.screenshot` / `debug.panel_snapshot` — they return mock/core-state output and are not routed on the live bridge. Real GTK pixel capture is out of scope.

tasks.title: Implement Live-Bridge Parity Core: ControlState Fall-Through with Method Registry, Mirror Sync, and Mutation Routing
tasks.description: Close the 18-vs-100+ method gap between the live GTK bridge and the standalone dispatcher by: (1) extracting a single-source-of-truth method registry with deny-by-default classification, (2) adding limux-core public API (shared-state constructor, pub sync dispatch, snapshot-import/sync on ControlState), (3) implementing a per-request clone-based read fall-through against a live-synced ControlState mirror with schema-aware id-rewrite, (4) routing Wave-1 mutation methods as ControlCommand variants on the GTK main loop, and (5) adding system.capabilities reporting. The registry is co-designed with lifo's Cursor PR #15 restricted surface so both parity routing and the Cursor allowlist consume one source of truth. Includes env kill-switch (LIMUX_BRIDGE_PARITY=0) for safe rollback.
tasks.details:
Execute in small, reviewed commits per PRD commit-decomposition (each commit passes ./scripts/check.sh + Xvfb smoke):

**Commit 1 — Registry extraction + deny-by-default (no behavior change):**
- Create `rust/limux-host-linux/src/control_registry.rs` (reuse limux-control crate location if lifo's PR #15 already created a registry home — do NOT duplicate).
- Define classification enum: `bridge-native | fallthrough-read | gtk-mutation | deferred | restricted`.
- Populate the table by READING each core method's implementation (lib.rs:882-909 confirms `workspace.next/previous/last` are MUTATION class because `select_workspace_relative`/`select_last_workspace` write selection state + mark notifications read — NOT by name).
- Wave-1 mutation set to classify as `gtk-mutation`: `pane.focus`, `pane.resize` (+ `resize-pane`), `surface.split` (+ split-direction args), `surface.focus`, `surface.close`, `workspace.reorder`, `workspace.next/previous/last`, `tab.action` (all existing actions), `notification.clear`.
- Read-only methods to classify as `fallthrough-read`: `workspace.list/current`, `window.list/current`, `pane.list/surfaces`, `surface.list/current/health`, `notification.list`, plus read legs of tmux-compat verbs (`find-window`, `list-buffers`, `display-message` resolution). `surface.read_text` stays `bridge-native`.
- Deferred mutations to classify as `deferred`: `pane.swap/break/join`, `surface.move/reorder/drag_to_split`, `workspace.move_to_window`, `window.create/close/focus`.
- All unclassified methods stay `-32601` (deny-by-default).
- Requires lifo or subagent lens review sign-off on the classification table.

**Commit 2a — limux-core public API (reviewed by lifo before 2b):**
- Add `Dispatcher::with_shared_state(Arc<Mutex<ControlState>>)` pub constructor (today only `Dispatcher::new` at lib.rs:2757 and `Dispatcher::with_state` at :2763 which consumes state by value into a NEW Arc<Mutex> — must accept an EXISTING shared Arc).
- Add pub SYNC dispatch entry point (today `Dispatcher::dispatch` at :2769 is `async` but body never awaits; bridge connection threads are sync, so a sync entry is required).
- Add pub snapshot-import/sync surface on `ControlState` so GTK state can be written into the mirror (today `ControlState` fields/methods are private; `dispatch_request` is private).
- This commit is a limux-core FR; lifo reviews before anything builds on it.

**Commit 2b — Mirror + sync + clone-per-read fall-through + id-rewrite layer:**
- Create `rust/limux-host-linux/src/state_mirror.rs` for mirror sync logic (pure-testable without GTK where feasible per docs/maintainability.md discipline).
- Document lock-discipline rule in `state_mirror.rs` header: NEVER hold the mirror mutex across a GTK main-loop dispatch (deadlock risk — bridge thread vs main loop).
- GTK app owns an `Arc<Mutex<ControlState>>` MIRROR kept in sync at mutation call sites in `window.rs` that already persist `layout_state` (e.g. window.rs:961 call sites): create/close/rename/focus/reorder/split.
- Bridge fall-through in `control_bridge.rs`: registry lookup → native | fallthrough (read) | ControlCommand (mutation) | -32601.
- CRITICAL INVARIANT: fall-through must be read-only — enforce via registry classification, deny-by-default. Binding mitigation: fall-through reads dispatch against a per-request CLONE of the mirror (`ControlState: Clone`, lib.rs:630). This avoids the read-path mutation contamination where `with_workspace_scope` (lib.rs:3118-3134) calls `select_workspace` on entry AND restore, unconditionally clobbering `last_workspace_id` and marking notifications read. The cost (cloning surface text buffers per control-plane request) is accepted and documented.
- ID mapping layer: dispatcher RESPONSES embed ids in three non-generic shapes — synthetic uuids via `encode_handle_id` ("00000000-…-{id:012x}", lib.rs:2847), `workspace:N`/`pane:N`/`surface:N` refs, and raw `u64` fields nested in serialized Info structs (`WorkspaceInfo`/`SurfaceInfo`, lib.rs:277-312 where a raw `id: 7` is indistinguishable from `flash_count: 7` generically). Implement schema-aware, per-method-family response id-rewrite: each fall-through family declares which response fields are ids and maps them to host-native id forms (host-linux uses `String` workspace ids, `u32` pane ids, uuid-`String` tab ids — repo CLAUDE.md pitfall). Wire-visible ids remain EXACTLY what today's bridge emits (no breaking change to refs/uuids id-format behavior).
- `SurfaceInfo.text` divergence: mirror-backed surface reads emit `text` as empty/omitted (mirror does not sync terminal text — hot path kept bridge-native via `surface.read_text`); documented + tested.
- `window.list` semantics: mirror exposes exactly one window per workspace, id = mapped host window (host-linux has no multi-window structure; core models windows-within-workspaces, lib.rs:286-291).
- No changes to socket framing, error codes, or existing 18 methods' wire shapes.

**Commit 3 — Mutation set (2–3 commits by family):**
- Each Wave-1 mutation method gets a `ControlCommand` variant executed on the GTK main loop (existing pattern for the 18 natives), updating both GUI and mirror atomically (single main-loop hop).
- Each mutation: follow-up read via fall-through reflects the mutation (test per method).
- Typed-PTY control-character guard and `send_text` readiness-conflict semantics unchanged (regression tests stay green).
- Deferred mutations explicitly classified `deferred` and still `-32601` — documented, not silently broken.

**Commit 4 — Capabilities reporting + docs + kill-switch:**
- `system.capabilities` reports the registry: method name → routing class, so agents can feature-detect.
- `LIMUX_BRIDGE_PARITY=0` env kill-switch: all fall-through + new mutation methods return `-32601` byte-identical to today, 18 natives unaffected. Checked once at bridge init (disabling requires GUI restart — accepted, documented). Regression test asserts exact byte-identical behavior when disabled.
- Cursor lane: method registry is one Rust source of truth that BOTH parity routing and Cursor-restricted allowlist consume. `integrations/cursor-limux/methods.json` generated from or verified against it by a Rust check-in-sync test (lands only AFTER PR #15 sequencing gate clears; methods.json currently names methods that exist only in lifo's unmerged PR #15 like `window.present`, `cursor.*`).
- `SocketControlMode`/auth behavior unchanged for non-restricted callers.
- Add `debug`-surface invariant check (mirror vs GUI walk) run in Xvfb smoke after every mutation family test (mirror-divergence is THE failure mode).
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing per PRD instructions:

1. **Unit tests:**
   - `cargo test -p limux-host-linux registry -- --nocapture` — registry classification tests, deny-by-default for unclassified methods (-32601 regression test).
   - `cargo test -p limux-host-linux state_mirror -- --nocapture` — pure-testable mirror sync logic without GTK where feasible.
   - `cargo test -p limux-host-linux bridge_fallthrough -- --nocapture` — bridge fall-through routing tests (native | fallthrough-read | ControlCommand-mutation | -32601).

2. **Xvfb smoke tests (extended):**
   - `LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh` — per-family live assertions + mirror-invariant check.
   - For each read family: Xvfb smoke assertion comparing bridge output vs mirror-dispatcher output for structural equality MODULO declared id-mapping and documented `text`-field divergence (raw equality not executable across two id vocabularies).
   - For each mutation in Wave-1 set: assert GUI AND mirror update atomically; follow-up read via fall-through reflects the mutation.
   - `debug`-surface invariant check (mirror vs GUI walk) after every mutation family test.
   - Typed-PTY control-character guard and `send_text` readiness-conflict semantics regression tests stay green.

3. **Kill-switch regression test:**
   - Assert `LIMUX_BRIDGE_PARITY=0` makes all fall-through + new mutation methods return `-32601` byte-identical to today; 18 natives unaffected.

4. **Coverage validation:**
   - Method-coverage table (generated from registry) shows 0 read-only methods unclassified; all Wave-1 mutation set live-routed.
   - tmux-compat verbs listed in US-2 work from inside a live pane on the operator's machine (PRD-C checklist addendum item).

5. **Each commit passes:** `./scripts/check.sh` (no NEW failures vs baseline) + Xvfb smoke.

tasks.title: Phase F1 — Architecture Decision Spike: WebKitGTK embedded pane vs CDP external browser
tasks.description: Evaluate the two browser-pane architecture candidates against WSL2-weighted criteria and produce the signed decision doc `docs/decisions/browser-pane-architecture-20260707.md`. This is a hard gate: no F2 implementation code may begin until the operator (or delegated lifo) signs off on the decision doc. Candidate (a) is the existing compiled-by-default WebKitGTK pane (runtime-gated today via `LIMUX_ENABLE_WEBKIT_BROWSER`); candidate (b) is CDP-driving an external Chromium-family browser. The spike must produce a scored matrix, prototype evidence for both candidates, and a recommendation, and must explicitly address the disposition of the shipped WebKit pane if (b) wins.
tasks.details:
## Scope

This task covers ONLY Phase F1 — architecture research, prototyping, measurement, and decision-doc production. No production code changes are in scope. All prototype code lives on throwaway spike branches and is NOT merged.

## Candidate (a) — WebKitGTK embedded pane (existing, runtime-gated)

The existing pane is compiled by default (`rust/limux-host-linux/Cargo.toml` default features include `webkit`, `webkit6 = "0.6"`). `BrowserHandles` in `pane.rs:~2871` contains the webview, url_entry, search bar, find controller, inspector/console handlers. It is GUI-wired via `window.rs:5221 on_open_browser_here`. WSLg GL mitigations are already applied in `configure_browser_settings` (sets `HardwareAccelerationPolicy`, pane.rs:~3195). `scripts/appimage-webkit.sh` bundles the WebKitWebProcess runtime.

Currently gated for normal users:
- `embedded_browser_enabled()` requires `LIMUX_ENABLE_WEBKIT_BROWSER` (`pane.rs:136-142`)
- Browser button hidden when false (`pane.rs:582-584`)
- `add_browser_tab_inner` returns early (`pane.rs:1414-1417`)

### Measurement plan for (a)

Evidence for (a) is measured on the existing pane with `LIMUX_ENABLE_WEBKIT_BROWSER=1` in a preview harness — NOT prototyped from scratch.

```bash
# Preview harness activation
export LIMUX_ENABLE_WEBKIT_BROWSER=1
export WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1  # if DMABUF crash class manifests
export WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 # if compositing crash manifests
# Test both GDK_BACKEND=wayland and GDK_BACKEND=x11
```

Measure:
1. **Memory at 3+ panes** — open 3+ browser panes with fixture pages; record RSS/PSS per pane and for the host process; compare against baseline (no browser panes).
2. **Subprocess/log hygiene** — open/close browser panes; verify WebKitWebProcess output does not interleave into `limux-host.log`; capture any noise on stderr into a separate stream.
3. **WSLg stability under existing `HardwareAccelerationPolicy` mitigation** — run scrolling + video-less page render for 10 minutes; check for DMABUF/compositing crashes under both Wayland and X11 GDK backends.
4. **Clipboard integration** — copy/paste into/from the webview under WSLg.
5. **IME/keyboard input** — type into web form fields; verify no key event loss.
6. **Scrolling + render performance** — scroll a long fixture page; measure frame timing / visual responsiveness (qualitative + any available metrics).

## Candidate (b) — CDP external browser

Limux launches or attaches to a Chromium-family browser via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) over localhost. Two rendering sub-variants must be scored independently:

1. **Managed external window** (v1-minimal, cheap): Limux owns control/automation via CDP but does not embed the browser visually; the external browser window is managed alongside the Limux GUI.
2. **CDP screencast-into-widget** (true pane, more work): Limux renders a live view of the remote browser by capturing CDP screencast frames into a GTK widget, forwarding input events back via CDP.

mux precedent: cmux #7325.

### Prototype plan for (b) — throwaway spike branch, NOT merged

Minimum viable prototype must demonstrate end-to-end under WSLg:

```rust
// SPIKE CODE — throwaway branch, not merged
// 1. Launch a Chromium-family browser with --remote-debugging-port=0
//    (or attach to an existing instance)
fn launch_or_attach_cdp_browser() -> Result<CdpSession> {
    let browser_executable = std::env::var("LIMUX_BROWSER_BIN")
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| which("chromium").or(which("google-chrome"))...);
    let port = find_free_localhost_port();
    Command::new(&browser_executable)
        .arg(format!("--remote-debugging-port={}", port))
        .arg("--no-first-run")
        .spawn()?;
    // Poll http://localhost:{port}/json/version until ready
    CdpSession::connect(format!("ws://localhost:{port}/..."))
}

// 2. Render a page via CDP Target.createTarget
// 3. Execute browser.navigate, browser.snapshot, browser.click
//    mapped to CDP commands:
//    - navigate  → Page.navigate
//    - snapshot  → Accessibility.getFullAXTree (or DOM.getDocument + outerHTML)
//    - click     → Input.dispatchMouseEvent (after DOM.resolveNode for selector)
// 4. For screencast sub-variant: Page.startScreencast → onScreencastFrame
//    → render frames into a GTK drawing area; measure FPS + input latency
```

Must test BOTH attach targets per Open Question 3:
- **Linux-side Chromium** launched from within WSL2
- **Windows-side Chrome** attached over the WSL2 localhost boundary

Measure for (b):
1. **Screencast sub-variant FPS + input latency** under software rendering
2. **Windows-Chrome attach: localhost forwarding across WSL2 boundary** — verify CDP port is reachable; measure latency
3. **Version-skew risk** — check whether CDP protocol version matches across Chrome versions; document graded criteria
4. **Memory footprint** — external browser process memory + Limux-side overhead at 3+ managed tabs
5. **Auth/profile reuse** — verify operator's real browser state is available (cookies, bookmarks, sessions) when attaching to the operator's own browser
6. **`browser.*` vocabulary coverage achievable** — map the Wave-1 method set to CDP equivalents and identify gaps
7. **Subprocess/log hygiene** — capture Chromium stderr output into its own stream
8. **Packaging weight** — no WebKitGTK dependency needed; instead document the "operator provides Chromium/Chrome path via `limux.browserExecutable` / `LIMUX_BROWSER_BIN`" convention (mirroring the Cursor lane's absolute-executable-path convention)

## Decision criteria (weights defined in the doc)

The decision doc must contain a scored matrix evaluating both candidates against:

1. **WSLg rendering stability** — including the WebKitGTK DMABUF/compositing crash class (`WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` / `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE`) and GDK backend choice (Wayland vs X11)
2. **WSLg clipboard integration + IME/keyboard input into the webview**
3. **Memory footprint at 3+ browser panes**
4. **Auth/profile reuse** (operator's real browser state)
5. **`browser.*` vocabulary coverage achievable**
6. **Subprocess/log hygiene**
7. **Packaging weight** (AppImage/AUR/RPM; `appimage-webkit.sh` bundles WebKitWebProcess today)
8. **Maintenance surface**
9. **For (b) screencast sub-variant: measured FPS + input-latency targets under software rendering**
10. **For (b) Windows-Chrome attach: localhost forwarding across WSL2 boundary + version-skew risk**

All criteria are graded (not open questions) with numeric weights and per-candidate scores.

## Mandatory decision-doc sections

### 1. Scored matrix
A table with each criterion, its weight, the score for each candidate (and sub-variant for (b)), and a weighted total.

### 2. Prototype evidence
Measured data from both prototypes: memory numbers, FPS/latency measurements, crash logs, clipboard/IME test results, vocabulary-coverage mapping.

### 3. Recommendation
A clear recommendation with rationale, including whether a v1 managed-window + v2 screencast ladder is appropriate for (b).

### 4. Existing-pane disposition (MANDATORY)
If (b) wins, the doc MUST specify what happens to the shipped WebKit pane:
- Remove the default cargo feature (`default = ["webkit"]`)?
- Coexist as GUI-only (keep WebKit for human users, CDP for agents)?
- Migrate fully to CDP?

Silence on this section is a **review-blocking gap**.

### 5. Open questions resolution
- **OQ1:** Allowlist default contents — propose: empty (deny-all) with the checklist walking the operator through adding their doc domains. Confirm at F1 gate.
- **OQ2:** Should audit events ALSO surface as `notification.create` for high-risk actions (script injection)? Default: log-only v1.
- **OQ3:** If F1 chooses CDP: attach to the operator's real Windows Chrome over the WSL2 boundary, or a Linux-side Chromium? The spike must test both; Windows-side attach has localhost-forwarding + version-skew risks.

### 6. Script/cookie/storage classification decision
The doc must decide whether `browser.addscript`/`addinitscript`/`addstyle` and `browser.cookies`/`storage` mutations are `deferred` in v1 (default — highest injection risk, lowest agent need) or argued in with a threat note.

## Output artifacts

1. `docs/decisions/browser-pane-architecture-20260707.md` — the decision doc with all sections above
2. Spike branch(es) with prototype code (not merged, tagged for reference)
3. Sign-off record (operator or delegated lifo) — can be a PR review approval or a signed commit

## Dependency note

Per the PRD: "Phase F1 (spike) can start before PRD-E completes; Phase F2 (implementation) cannot." This task has no blocking dependencies on PRD-E. The gate is sign-off on the decision doc, which is a review/approval step, not a code dependency.

tasks.title: Implement agent lifecycle state machine, hook integration, sidebar rendering, and socket exposure
tasks.description: Create a pure, unit-testable agent lifecycle state machine module, fix per-family hook installer mappings, wire hook shims to emit surface.agent_event control calls, render aggregated workspace state in sidebar rows with targeted updates, expose agent_state over the control socket, and add the agents-status CLI convenience — all per PRD-G.
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing follows the PRD's testing instructions and acceptance criteria across three layers:

**Unit tests** (`cargo test -p limux-host-linux agent_state -- --nocapture`):
- State machine: all transitions per the state model table (unknown→running→needs-input→idle and back to running on next event).
- Aggregation logic: any needs-input → needs-input; else any running → running; else any idle → idle; else unknown.
- Eviction on surface/pane/tab close (Codex-required — closed surface stuck in needs-input must not pin workspace aggregate).
- Stale-state decay: running → unknown after configurable period (default 30 min) using injected clock (no sleeps).
- Operator interaction does NOT mutate state; acknowledged bit clears on focus.
- Socket-reported state and sidebar never disagree.

**CLI/integration tests** (`cargo test -p limux-cli hooks_agent_event -- --nocapture`):
- Hook shim emits surface.agent_event as second fire-and-forget call after notification.create.
- Connect+write timeout 2 s, failures silent.
- surface.agent_event additive and classified as mutation.
- Fixture hook payloads per family (claude, codex, gemini, opencode, hermes) — reuse payload shapes the hook shims already parse.

**Xvfb smoke test** (`LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh` — extended):
- Fake-agent lifecycle: state transitions arrive without focus changes (background workspace row updates when agent stops).
- Rebuild counter: push 100 state updates across 20 workspaces, assert debug counter == 0 (no row re-creation, no full sidebar_list repopulation).
- 8-combination visual matrix: {needs-input indicator on|off} × {unread dot on|off} × {attention border on|off} — assert widget/CSS-class presence structurally.
- One rendering assertion each for running, idle, and unknown indicator variants.
- Batching: 50-event burst within one frame coalesces to one row update.
- Wall-time recorded for 100-update scenario (target: no worse than 2× single-update cost; include in PR description).

**Full suite**:
```bash
./scripts/check.sh
cargo test -p limux-host-linux agent_state -- --nocapture
cargo test -p limux-cli hooks_agent_event -- --nocapture
LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh
```

**Manual/PRD-C checklist addendum**: with 3 concurrent agents, sidebar correctly shows which one is waiting on input within ~2 s of the agent stopping.

tasks.title: Implement Session Restore Correctness Pack: round-trip tests, cwd inheritance, recently-closed & focus history
tasks.description: Implement the full PRD-H scope across three areas: (1) Verify split geometry/identity round-trip fidelity via full-layout save→restore tests and a kill/restart Xvfb harness; fix corrupt-file clobbering. (2) Add cwd inheritance on split via a shared resolution helper (term_cwd → workspace cwd → $HOME) across GUI, bridge, and core split paths. (3) Add recently-closed ring buffer (workspace/tab), focus-history back/forward navigation, CLI verbs, default keybinds, GUI submenu, and persistence in session.json with additive serde fields.
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing is organized by track, matching the PRD's Testing Instructions block.

### Track 1: Round-trip & Corrupt-File
```bash
cargo test -p limux-host-linux layout_roundtrip -- --nocapture
```
- `layout_round_trip_preserves_structure_and_metadata`: 3-workspace fixture, H/V nested splits, non-default ratios, pinned/renamed tabs, cross-pane duplicate tab ids — assert normalized-snapshot equivalence (order, orientation, ratios ±0.5%, pane_id, active_tab_id, title, pinned, unread).
- `layout_round_trip_preserves_flag_color` (feature-gated): assert pane-scoped `flag_color` if PRD-D merged.
- `atomic_save_writes_temp_then_renames`: verify `save_session_atomic_in` path.
- `corrupt_file_preserved_before_default`: load corrupt session.json → assert `session.json.corrupt-<ts>` exists + one log line; state is default.
- `cross_version_fixture_loads_and_drops_new_fields`: older build loads newer file (serde unknown-field tolerance), drops new fields on save.
- `restored_pane_cwd_regression`: verify existing `snapshot_pane_state` → `cwd.as_deref().or(working_directory)` path (US-2).

**Xvfb harness (integration):**
```bash
LIMUX_SMOKE_PROFILE=debug ./scripts/xvfb-smoke-test.sh
```
- Second-launch mode: kill/restart, same session dir, snapshot diff, assert normalized equivalence + split ratios at drag-adjusted values + split-cwd assertion for deep-cwd pane.

### Track 2: cwd Inheritance
```bash
cargo test -p limux-host-linux cwd_inheritance -- --nocapture
```
- `split_inherits_source_term_cwd`: fixture pane whose shell cd'd post-spawn; split inherits new dir (cmux #7155 case).
- `explicit_cwd_always_wins`: pass explicit `--cwd`; assert it overrides helper resolution.
- `fallback_chain_term_cwd_workspace_home`: unit test `resolve_split_cwd` with all combinations.
- `new_workspace_behavior_unchanged`: test pins workspace-level cwd semantics.
- `cwd_inheritance_lands_in_all_three_paths`: test GUI `split_pane`, bridge `pane.create`, core `surface.split`.

### Track 3: Recently-Closed & Focus History
```bash
cargo test -p limux-host-linux recent_closed -- --nocapture
cargo test -p limux-core focus_history -- --nocapture
```
- `recently_closed_ring_push_cap_and_list`: ring caps at 20, oldest evicted, list returns in order.
- `recently_closed_persists_across_restart`: save → load → entries preserved; ring caps enforced on load.
- `recently_closed_serialized_size_under_256kb`: assert serialized size <256KB.
- `reopen_closed_restores_workspace_layout_snapshot`: workspace reopen restores structure; terminal processes start fresh.
- `focus_history_back_forward_navigation`: push user-selects; back/forward navigate correctly.
- `focus_history_ignores_programmatic_selects`: restore-time select storm does NOT push history.
- `focus_history_persists_across_restart`: additive fields load/save round-trip.
- `workspace_back_forward_return_32601_when_unclassified`: rollback safety (methods unclassified → error).
- Headless core dispatcher tests for `workspace.back/forward` mirror registrations.

### General
```bash
./scripts/check.sh
```
- Lints, formatting, existing tests still pass.
- Contributor-docs note present (pane-local tab ids valid across panes; `normalize_pane_tab_ids` within-one-pane only).
